0.0.n: 時 marks the hour and 半 adds half an hour; morning is understood from context.

1.0.n: Links this action to what happened before.

1.1.n: Sets the frequency of the drinking habit without needing a particle.

1.2.n: 杯 counts cupfuls or glassfuls; 一杯 is read いっぱい.

1.3.n: Connects the quantity 一杯 to the drink ハーブティー.

1.4.n: A borrowed expression written in katakana, combining ハーブ and ティー.

1.5.n: Marks the cup of herbal tea as what the speaker drinks.

1.6.n: The polite form of 飲む describes a regular habit here.

2.0.n: Refers back to drinking herbal tea.

2.1.n: Marks the preceding action as what makes a pleasant morning possible.

2.2.n: A な-adjective describing a fresh, pleasant feeling, used with に here to describe spending the morning.

2.3.n: Turns 爽やか into a description of how the speaker spends the morning.

2.4.n: Names the period of time being spent.

2.5.n: Marks 朝 as the time period that 過ごす acts on.

2.6.n: The dictionary form comes before こと to make spending the morning into an activity that can be discussed.

2.7.n: Turns the preceding action into a noun-like phrase so it can connect to ができます.

2.8.n: Marks the whole activity expressed before こと as what is possible.

2.9.n: The polite form of できる; after a verb plus ことが, it expresses being able to do that action.

0.tip: Add 半 after an hour with 時 to mean thirty minutes past that hour.

1.lit: Then, every morning, one cup of herbal tea, I drink.
1.tip: 毎朝 makes 飲みます a regular habit rather than an action happening right now.

2.lit: Thanks to this, spending the morning in a refreshed way is possible.
2.tip: A dictionary-form verb followed by ことができます means can do that action.
